```plato
//==
// # Quantities - the measured-amount interface
//
// A quantity is a number with an intrinsic unit of measure implied by its type
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physical_quantity). Quantities add, subtract,
// scale, order, and interpolate - but multiplying two quantities yields a
// different type, so they are deliberately not IArithmetic. Each implementing
// type's field name states its canonical (SI or conventional) unit
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/International_System_of_Units). The concrete
// types live in `quantities.types.plato`; the obligation fills that make
// them usable live in `quantities.library.plato`.

// A one-dimensional measured amount with an implicit unit.
interface IQuantity
    inherits IValue, IComparable, IHashable, IAdditive, IScalable, IInterpolatable
{
    Amount(x: Self): Number;
    FromAmount(_: Self, x: Number): Self;
}
```
